extracted.intended_audience: mathematical physicists and differential geometers working on geometric quantization, BRST quantization, and symplectic reduction
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, necessary conditions, and constructions for prequantization data, polarizations, and the BRST (classical and quantum) constructions on symplectic manifolds; includes conditions for induced data on reduced spaces and for cohomological/inner-product properties. Focused on producing/validating geometric-quantization and BRST structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrality / prequantizability of the symplectic form
rubrics_metrics.description: Ω is integral if its de Rham class lies in the image of H^2(M;Z)→H^2(M;R); equivalently (M,Ω) is prequantizable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Ω is integral then there exists at least one complex line bundle E→M with a Hermitian structure and a connection ∇ whose curvature satisfies curv(∇) = −2π i Ω; the triple (E,∇,⟨·,·⟩) are the prequantum data. This is the basic necessary condition to begin geometric prequantization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prequantum line bundle properties (PQ1, PQ2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of a Hermitian structure ⟨·,·⟩ on sections and a connection ∇ such that (PQ1) the pointwise inner product is parallel (d⟨σ,τ⟩ = ⟨σ,∇τ⟩+⟨∇σ,τ⟩) and (PQ2) curvature equals −2π i Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These two properties define a valid prequantum line bundle: (PQ1) ensures compatibility of the metric and connection; (PQ2) ties the connection curvature to the symplectic form. Use these to build the prequantum Hilbert space by L^2-completion with respect to the Liouville measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prequantization map and representation of Poisson algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Define O(f) = ∇_{X_f} + 2π i f for f ∈ C^∞(M); this map satisfies [O(f),O(g)] = O({f,g}) and O(f)(gσ) = {f,g}σ + g O(f)σ and each O(f) is skew-symmetric (and for complete X_f gives skew-self-adjoint extensions generating unitaries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prequantization map must represent the Poisson algebra on the prequantum Hilbert space, be (formally) skew-adjoint with correct commutators, and the only operators commuting with all O(g) are scalar multiples of identity (highly reducible representation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a polarization
rubrics_metrics.description: A polarization F is an involutive, Lagrangian, complex subbundle of the complexified tangent bundle TC M (i.e., F_m ⊂ TC_m M is a complex Lagrangian subspace and Γ(F) is involutive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polarizations come in types: real (F = ), totally complex (F ∩ F̄ = 0) and positive-definite (g(X,Y)=Ω(X, JY) positive definite making (M,J) Kähler). The canonical polarization of a cotangent bundle is the real polarization given by the kernel of the projection.

rubrics_metrics.name: AF and NF function classes relative to a polarization
rubrics_metrics.description: AF = {f ∈ C^∞_C(M) | X_f = 0 ∀ X ∈ Γ(F)}; equivalently functions whose Hamiltonian vector fields lie in Γ(F). NF = {f ∈ C^∞_C(M) | {X_f, Y} ∈ Γ(F) ∀ Y ∈ Γ(F)} (normalizer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AF is an abelian Poisson subalgebra (and sometimes maximal abelian); NF is a Lie subalgebra stabilizing Γ_F(E) and contains AF as an abelian ideal. In practice only (real) functions in NF are readily quantizable on the polarized Hilbert space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polarized sections and quantum Hilbert space construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Γ_F(E) = {σ ∈ Γ(E) | ∇_X σ = 0 ∀ X ∈ Γ(F)}; the quantum Hilbert space is the L^2-completion of polarized sections of finite norm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If F is totally complex and positive-definite, Γ_F(E) are holomorphic sections and one expects L^2-holomorphic sections; if polarization is not positive-definite there may be no L^2 polarized sections (exponential growth), which motivates restricting to positive-definite polarizations or introducing half-form corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Half-form correction for integrability
rubrics_metrics.description: When polarized sections are not L^2 (e.g., non-compact leaves or non-positive polarizations), tensor the prequantum line bundle with a bundle of half-forms so that pointwise inner products yield integrable forms on the leaf space M/D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Half-form quantization naturally yields objects integrable on the appropriate quotient; this can overcome non-compactness/exponential-growth obstructions to obtaining finite-norm polarized sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Koszul resolution and inducing bundles to constrained/reduced spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 is a regular value of Φ: M → R^k and E → M is a vector bundle, the Koszul complex K(Φ; Γ(E)) gives an acyclic resolution of Γ(E)/JΓ(E) and identifies Γ(i^{-1}E) with Γ(E)/JΓ(E) (i: Φ^{-1}(0) → M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This algebraic Koszul construction provides the bridge to lift sections from M to the constraint submanifold and, via vertical cohomology, to the quotient bundle over the reduced manifold. It is the algebraic heart of the BRST induction of prequantum data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poisson-module structure compatibility for Γ(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Γ(E) must be a Poisson module over C^∞(M): there is an action (f,σ) ↦ f × σ satisfying (M1)-(M3): module over associative product, Lie action property, and derivation rule a×(b·m) = {a,b}·m + (−1)^{|a||b|} b·(a×m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice this is realized when E has a (flat) connection and f × σ = ∇_{X_f} σ (or via Lie derivative); these properties are necessary to lift the Poisson/BRST structures to K(E) and to define D = {Q,·} on modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariant polarization under group or constraints action
rubrics_metrics.description: A polarization F is G-invariant (or invariant under first-class constraints {φ_i}) iff the induced action on TC M preserves F; equivalently for connected G, {φ_X, Y} ∈ Γ(F) for all Y ∈ Γ(F) (or φ_i ∈ NF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G-invariance ensures F_o = F ∩ TC M_o descends to an involutive Lagrangian subbundle on the reduced manifold and that polarized sections form g-modules. Invariant polarizations can impose strong conditions on the allowed constraints (e.g., linearity in momenta for canonical real polarization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constraints leaving canonical real polarization invariant must be linear in momenta
rubrics_metrics.description: For the canonical real polarization ker π_* on T^*N, the condition that a Hamiltonian X_f stabilizes the polarization yields ∂^2 f / ∂p_a ∂p_b = 0, hence f is linear in the momenta.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: such constraints have flows that induce well-defined transformations on configuration space; structure functions become independent of momenta and induce functions on the base N, simplifying BRST charge structure (only linear and trilinear ghost terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of ghost polarization to stabilize BRST operator
rubrics_metrics.description: To have the BRST operator D_∇ preserve the polarized complex one must polarize the ghost sector so that only the appropriate subspace (e.g., ∧ V^* rather than ∧(V^*⊕V)) remains; otherwise terms like φ_k σ will not be polarized (require φ_k ∈ AF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In totally complex polarizations, φ_k (real non-constant) cannot be holomorphic so D_∇ does not stabilize unless ghosts are polarized. For group actions with AF maximal, one is forced to polarize ghosts so the surviving BRST piece is ∇_1 and the quantum BRST complex becomes ∧^• V^* ⊗ Γ_F(E) with differential ∇_1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for inner product to descend to BRST cohomology (unimodularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the inner product on the BRST complex to descend to cohomology one needs ∑_{i,j} f_{i j}{}^j = 0 for all i (equivalently tr(ad b_i)=0), i.e., the Lie algebra g is unimodular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition ensures ∇_1 is (up to sign) formally self-adjoint on integrable elements so coboundaries are orthogonal to cocycles and hence the induced inner product on cohomology is well-defined. It is physically desirable (gauge-related states equivalent) though the induced inner product may not be the physical one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ghost-number operator shift for skew-adjointness / Hodge decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: To make the ghost-number operator skew-adjoint one must shift it by c = k/2 (for k ghosts), i.e., N_c = N − k/2; with this shift and a positive-definite polarization one can define adjoints and a BRST Laplacian leading to a Hodge decomposition and duality H_n ≅ H_{−n}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This normal-ordering/shift is necessary for the inner product to have the expected symmetry between positive and negative ghost numbers; it is used in the construction of a positive-definite inner product on the complex K_F(E) and in proving duality theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Berezin integral and inner product on ghost sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Fix a nonzero top-form ε ∈ ∧^k V^* and define the Berezin integral !Ber with !Ber(ε) = 1 and !Ber of lower-degree forms = 0. Define inner product on forms by ⟨ω,θ⟩ = (−i)^p (k−p)! !Ber(ω ∧ θ) for ω ∈ ∧^p V^*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the specified factors (−i)^p (k−p)! to secure the hermiticity properties needed for the BRST operator and to combine with the matter inner product (L^2 prequantum inner product) to produce a positive-definite inner product on integrable elements of K_F(E).
